name: Subterrains
description: Splits the map's terrain and placed objects into subterrains (map/terrain/: one folder per rectangle, so several people can edit different parts of a large map and merge in git), and merges them back into the single files. The map is the same either way; every editor reads and saves it as before. Open Subterrains… (and the Subterrains view) opens only some of them: the others aren't read, drawn or saved, and a strip of two corners around the open ones is shown read-only.

mcpTools.name: check_terrain_seams
mcpTools.description: Check Terrain Seams of a split terrain (map/terrain/): the saved terrain, every subterrain read, checked where two subterrains meet with the terrain brushes' rules (cliffs of more than two levels, ramp flags that don't climb one level, water that steps in a tile). Lists every corner the rules would change, with its subterrain; changes nothing. Errors stop `w3proj pack`.

mcpTools.name: change_subterrains
mcpTools.description: New, Resize, Rename or Join Subterrains of a split terrain (map/terrain/), as the palette commands do it: the map stays the same, only which subterrain file holds what changes (terrain, objects by position, regions, pathing overrides); folders follow the names, creation-number ranges are kept (a join keeps all, a new one gets the next block). action "new" needs name and rect, "resize" name and rect, "rename" name and to, "join" names (two or more side by side) and to. rect is "x,y,w,h" in corners, (0,0) the south-west corner. A rectangle takes a whole side off the subterrains it covers (or all of one). Refused, nothing changed, while anything is unsaved, when one would be cut in pieces, when a corner left out differs from the default corner, or for a bad name. Answers what was written and removed and the subterrains afterwards.

mcpTools.name: fix_creation_ids
mcpTools.description: Creation numbers (editorId; what scripts call gg_unit_hfoo_0012, gg_dest_…) found more than once among the placed doodads, units or regions, flat or split project, each with every object holding it (file, index, type, position, exact copies). Without apply only the plan: mode "renumber" gives every object of a number but the first the next free number (a split terrain: in its subterrain's idRange); mode "deleteCopies" removes only objects that are exact copies of an earlier one, those that differ stay and are listed. With apply: true and a mode it is done as one undoable edit; refused while anything is unsaved. Split and pack never renumber on their own.
